name: Upgrade Template
summary: The blank card every upgrade in the mod starts from, made on a Create sequenced assembly line from a copper sheet.

teach.what: A copper sheet that has had a Cogwheel, Glass and an Electron Tube deployed onto it in a sequenced assembly. On its own it does nothing: it's the base you finish into a Wellspring upgrade or a chest upgrade.
teach.why: Every [[fluid-wellspring]] upgrade and every [[chest-upgrades|chest upgrade]] begins here, so it's the first thing to automate.
teach.when: As soon as you can run a sequenced assembly line: a belt or depot with Deployers, and a supply of Electron Tubes.
teach.interacts: Finish it into a [[capacity-upgrade]] (three Fluid Tanks), a [[drip-template]] (two Pointed Dripstone, for the water, lava, honey and chocolate upgrades) or a [[chest-upgrade-template]] (a chest and Andesite Alloy).
mistakes: Feeding the Deployers in the wrong order. The sequence is Cogwheel, then Glass, then Electron Tube; the Incomplete Upgrade Template only moves on with the right part.
Taking an Incomplete Upgrade Template off the line by hand: it's useless until the sequence finishes.

specs: Deploy Cogwheel, deploy Glass, deploy Electron Tube
obtain: Sequenced assembly on a copper sheet: deploy a Cogwheel, then any glass block, then an Electron Tube. One pass, no loops.
The Incomplete Upgrade Template is the item in between steps.
uses: Three Fluid Tanks deployed onto it make a [[capacity-upgrade]].
Two Pointed Dripstone deployed onto it make a [[drip-template]].
A chest and Andesite Alloy deployed onto it make a [[chest-upgrade-template]].
tips: Build one sequenced assembly line for the template, then a second line for whatever you finish it into. A Deployer swap is all that changes.
facts: Your first one earns Template Monkey: "Every great invention starts as a blank card".

flows.title: From a copper sheet to every upgrade

name: Chest Upgrade Template
summary: An Upgrade Template with a chest and Andesite Alloy deployed onto it: the base of the Copper Chest Upgrade.

teach.what: The middle step between an [[upgrade-template]] and your first [[chest-upgrades|chest upgrade]].
teach.why: Every chest tier is built on the one before, and they all start from this template.
teach.when: Right after your first Upgrade Template.
teach.interacts: Two copper sheets deployed onto it, then a press, make a Copper Chest Upgrade.
mistakes: Trying to use it on a chest. It isn't an upgrade yet: finish it with copper sheets first.
Loading the Deployers the wrong way round. The chest goes on first, then the Andesite Alloy.

specs: Deploy a wooden chest, deploy Andesite Alloy
obtain: Sequenced assembly on an [[upgrade-template]]: deploy a wooden chest, then Andesite Alloy.
uses: Deploy two copper sheets onto it and press it: a Copper Chest Upgrade.
facts: Making one earns Never Skip Chest Day.
tips: Keep a few spare: every chest tier starts from one, and a stack of templates lets you upgrade a whole storage room in one go.

name: Drip Template
summary: An Upgrade Template fitted with two Pointed Dripstone, ready to be finished with a fluid into a Wellspring generation upgrade.

teach.what: The base of every generation upgrade for the [[fluid-wellspring]]. A Spout fills it with 250 mB of water or lava to make a [[water-upgrade]] or [[lava-upgrade]]; a longer sequence turns it into a [[honey-upgrade]] or [[chocolate-upgrade]].
teach.why: One template line feeds all four generation upgrades, so you only need to change the fluid.
teach.when: Straight after your first Upgrade Template, on the way to an endless water or lava source.
teach.interacts: Spouts fill it (Create's filling). The honey and chocolate sequences take it as their starting item.
mistakes: Spouting the wrong amount: it takes exactly 250 mB of water or lava for the basic upgrades.
Spouting honey or chocolate straight onto it. Those upgrades need the full three-loop sequence, not a single fill.

obtain: Sequenced assembly on an [[upgrade-template]]: deploy Pointed Dripstone twice.
uses: Spout 250 mB of water onto it: a [[water-upgrade]].
Spout 250 mB of lava onto it: a [[lava-upgrade]].
The start of the three-loop [[honey-upgrade]] and [[chocolate-upgrade]] sequences.
tips: One Spout can make both Water and Lava Upgrades: just swap the fluid feeding it.

name: Water Upgrade
summary: A hydraulic module for the Fluid Wellspring: each one installed makes it generate water faster, up to 500 mB a second with three.

teach.what: Fitted to a [[fluid-wellspring]], it makes the tank fill itself with water: 100 mB a second with one, 250 with two, 500 with three.
teach.why: An endless water source in one block, with no pump and no infinite pool. It feeds [[fish-tank|Fish Tanks]], [[flooded-monster-cage|Flooded cages]], Create's washing fans and the [[geothermal-turbine]].
teach.when: Your first goal after the Upgrade Template. Water is useful everywhere.
teach.interacts: Pipes, pumps and [[fluid-lines|Fluid Lines]] (with an [[intake]]) draw from the Wellspring on any side. It can share the Wellspring with [[capacity-upgrade|Capacity Upgrades]], which have their own slots.
mistakes: Mixing kinds. A Wellspring takes one kind of generation upgrade at a time; empty it of its current fluid before you switch kinds.
Opening the upgrade screen with sneak + empty hand. That's Carry On's pickup; use a Wrench.
Expecting a fourth upgrade to help: three of one kind is the maximum.

obtain: A Spout fills a [[drip-template]] with 250 mB of water.
uses: Right-click a [[fluid-wellspring]] with it to install it; the Wrench screen adds and removes upgrades.
Each one plugs into a socket on the Wellspring's lid, with a lens in its fluid's colour.
tips: Two Water Upgrades make 250 mB a second: exactly what a [[geothermal-turbine]] boils off at full power.
facts: Fitting one earns Make It Rain: "Hydration on tap!"

name: Lava Upgrade
summary: A geothermal module for the Fluid Wellspring: each one installed makes it generate lava faster, up to 50 mB a second with three.

teach.what: Fitted to a [[fluid-wellspring]], it makes the tank fill itself with lava: 10 mB a second with one, 25 with two, 50 with three. (Its game id is still `dripstone_upgrade`.)
teach.why: Endless lava is fuel. It runs [[magma-engine|Magma Engines]], [[lava-generator|Lava Generators]] and the [[geothermal-turbine]], feeds the netherrack mixer for [[netherite-dust]], and meets water in the [[cobblestone-generator|stone generators]]' world.
teach.when: Early, alongside or just after water. It's the start of every power setup in the mod.
teach.interacts: A Lava Wellspring next to a Honey or Chocolate one makes Create's limestone or scoria where the fluids meet. Draw from it with pipes, pumps or [[fluid-lines|Fluid Lines]] and an [[intake]].
mistakes: Mixing kinds. A Wellspring takes one kind of generation upgrade at a time; empty it of its current fluid before you switch kinds.
Opening the upgrade screen with sneak + empty hand. That's Carry On's pickup; use a Wrench.
Under-supplying a big consumer. One fully upgraded Lava Wellspring (50 mB/s) runs a [[magma-engine]] (10 mB/s) five times over, but a [[geothermal-turbine]] needs 90 mB/s: two maxed Wellsprings.

obtain: A Spout fills a [[drip-template]] with 250 mB of lava.
uses: Right-click a [[fluid-wellspring]] with it to install it.
Size your fuel: a [[lava-generator]] burns 20 mB/s, a [[magma-engine]] 10, a [[supercharged-magma-engine]] 20, a [[geothermal-turbine]] 90 at full power.
tips: A maxed Lava Wellspring (50 mB/s) keeps two and a half Lava Generators burning flat out.
facts: Fitting one earns The Floor Is Lava: "Mind your toes".

name: Capacity Upgrade
summary: A reinforced tank module that makes a Fluid Wellspring hold 16,000 mB more, in its own slots beside the generation upgrades.

teach.what: Each one adds 16,000 mB to a [[fluid-wellspring]]'s 8,000 mB tank, up to three: 56,000 mB in all. It shows as a copper canister in the lid's back row.
teach.why: A bigger tank rides out bursts of demand, such as a [[magma-engine]] starting up or a [[fish-tank]] breeding a whole school at once, and stores more for when nothing is drawing.
teach.when: Once your Wellspring keeps running dry under load, or fills up and stops between uses.
teach.interacts: It has its own slots, so it goes alongside Water, Lava, Honey or Chocolate Upgrades without counting against them.
mistakes: Taking one out of a full tank. It's refused until you drain the Wellspring to what the smaller tank can hold.
Expecting it to make fluid faster. It only adds room; generation comes from the generation upgrades.

obtain: Sequenced assembly on an [[upgrade-template]]: deploy three Fluid Tanks.
uses: Right-click a [[fluid-wellspring]] with it to install it.
facts: Fitting one earns Tank You Very Much: "Room for seconds".
tips: Fit Capacity Upgrades to the Wellsprings that feed bursty machines; a steady consumer only needs generation.

name: Honey Upgrade
summary: A Wellspring upgrade that generates Create's honey, 10 to 50 mB a second: next to a Lava Wellspring, an endless limestone source.

teach.what: Fitted to a [[fluid-wellspring]], it generates Create's honey: 10, 25 or 50 mB a second with one, two or three.
teach.why: Honey meets lava as limestone (Create's own fluid interaction), so a Honey Wellspring beside a Lava one is an endless limestone source. It's also honey on tap for Create's recipes.
teach.when: Mid game: each one costs three Precision Mechanisms and 3,000 mB of honey.
teach.interacts: Pair it with a [[lava-upgrade|Lava Wellspring]] for limestone. Pipes and [[fluid-lines|Fluid Lines]] draw it like any fluid.
mistakes: Mixing kinds. A Wellspring takes one kind of generation upgrade at a time; empty it of its current fluid before you switch kinds.
Opening the upgrade screen with sneak + empty hand. That's Carry On's pickup; use a Wrench.
Stopping the sequence early. It takes three full loops of four steps.

specs: 3 Honeycomb Blocks, 3,000 mB honey, 3 Precision Mechanisms
obtain: Sequenced assembly on a [[drip-template]], **3 loops** of: deploy a Honeycomb Block, spout 1,000 mB of honey, deploy a Precision Mechanism, press.
uses: Right-click a [[fluid-wellspring]] with it to install it.
tips: Put the Honey Wellspring right beside a Lava one so the two fluids meet in the world: Create turns the meeting into limestone you can mine with a drill.

name: Chocolate Upgrade
summary: A Wellspring upgrade that generates Create's chocolate, 10 to 50 mB a second: next to a Lava Wellspring, an endless scoria source.

teach.what: Fitted to a [[fluid-wellspring]], it generates Create's chocolate: 10, 25 or 50 mB a second with one, two or three.
teach.why: Chocolate meets lava as scoria (Create's own fluid interaction), so a Chocolate Wellspring beside a Lava one is an endless scoria source, and chocolate on tap for Create's sweets.
teach.when: Mid game, like the [[honey-upgrade]]: it costs three Precision Mechanisms each.
teach.interacts: Pair it with a [[lava-upgrade|Lava Wellspring]] for scoria.
mistakes: Mixing kinds. A Wellspring takes one kind of generation upgrade at a time; empty it of its current fluid before you switch kinds.
Opening the upgrade screen with sneak + empty hand. That's Carry On's pickup; use a Wrench.
Stopping the sequence early. It takes three full loops of four steps.

specs: 3 Cocoa Beans, 3,000 mB chocolate, 3 Precision Mechanisms
obtain: Sequenced assembly on a [[drip-template]], **3 loops** of: deploy Cocoa Beans, spout 1,000 mB of chocolate, deploy a Precision Mechanism, press.
uses: Right-click a [[fluid-wellspring]] with it to install it.
tips: As with honey, a Chocolate Wellspring touching a Lava one gives endless scoria where they meet.

name: Chest Upgrades
summary: Copper, Iron, Gold, Diamond and Netherite upgrades that turn a chest or barrel into a bigger one, each tier built on the last.

teach.what: Right-click a chest or barrel with one and it becomes an [[upgraded-chest]] or [[upgraded-barrel]], keeping its items. Copper doubles each slot, Iron quadruples it, Gold makes it eight times; Diamond keeps Gold's stacks and doubles the slots; Netherite has Diamond's slots, sixteen times the stack, and shrugs off explosions.
teach.why: Storage is the first thing a Create base runs out of. Each tier multiplies what one block holds, so funnels and arms have fewer chests to serve.
teach.when: Copper as soon as you have a [[chest-upgrade-template]]. Each tier after that only needs the previous upgrade and a little of the next metal, so climb as you can afford it. Netherite needs a Netherite Upgrade smithing template.
teach.interacts: Hoppers, funnels, arms and Pipez fill the upgraded slots to their limit. Upgraded chests keep their stacks on contraptions and Aeronautics ships, and Carry On carries them.
mistakes: Making two for a double chest. One upgrade covers both halves.
Trying to skip a tier. Each upgrade is made from the one below it, so a Gold upgrade needs an Iron one.
Downgrading a chest full of big stacks: it's refused until they'd fit.

specs: Vanilla chests and barrels, and lower-tier upgraded ones
Copper, Iron, Gold and Netherite stack multipliers (Diamond uses Gold's)

variants.name: Copper Chest Upgrade
variants.summary: x2 stacks: 128 a slot. Two copper sheets deployed onto a Chest Upgrade Template, then pressed.

variants.name: Iron Chest Upgrade
variants.summary: x4 stacks: 256 a slot. Two iron sheets deployed onto a Copper Chest Upgrade, then pressed.

variants.name: Gold Chest Upgrade
variants.summary: x8 stacks: 512 a slot. Two golden sheets deployed onto an Iron Chest Upgrade, then pressed.

variants.name: Diamond Chest Upgrade
variants.summary: Gold's 512 a slot with twice the slots. Two diamonds deployed onto a Gold Chest Upgrade, then pressed.

variants.name: Netherite Chest Upgrade
variants.summary: x16 stacks with Diamond's slots, and blast-proof. Smithed like netherite gear: a Netherite Upgrade template, a Diamond Chest Upgrade and a netherite ingot.
specs: Blast-proof chest; the item survives fire and lava

obtain: Copper: sequenced assembly on a [[chest-upgrade-template]], deploying two copper sheets, then pressing.
Iron, Gold and Diamond: the same on the previous tier's upgrade, with two iron sheets, two golden sheets or two diamonds.
Netherite: a smithing table with a Netherite Upgrade smithing template, a Diamond Chest Upgrade and a netherite ingot.
uses: Right-click a chest or barrel to upgrade it. Using a higher tier on an upgraded one replaces the upgrade and hands back the old one.
Use a Wrench (or sneak + right-click with an upgrade) on an upgraded chest to open its upgrade screen.
Sneak + right-click the side of a single upgraded chest with a chest to extend it into a double of the same tier.
tips: Old upgrades aren't wasted: when you climb a tier you get the previous upgrade back, ready for the next chest.
Netherite is the end of the line, worth it for storage near explosions.
facts: The tiers' advancements run Copper-Bottomed Guarantee, Pumping Iron, Heart of Gold, Bigger on the Inside and Ancient Debris Storage.

name: Emerald Dust
summary: Glittering green powder, a rare extra from crushing or milling cobblestone and stone: nine press into an Emerald.

teach.what: A by-product. Crushing Wheels turning cobblestone or stone into gravel have a 5% chance of Emerald Dust; a Millstone has 2.5%. Nine in a [[pressure-crucible]] over a heated Blaze Burner make one Emerald.
teach.why: It turns a [[cobblestone-generator]] into an emerald mine, with no villagers involved.
teach.when: As soon as you crush cobblestone. You'll collect dust long before you can press it, so start storing it.
teach.interacts: Feed it to the [[pressure-crucible]]. Spend the Emeralds on villager trades, or press a few more for [[trade-bot|Trade Bot]]'s Emerald Block.
mistakes: Pressing it over an unheated or smouldering burner. Emeralds need a **heated** Blaze Burner.
Milling when you could crush: a Millstone gives half the chance of Crushing Wheels.

obtain: Crushing Wheels on cobblestone or stone: 5% a block, alongside the gravel.
A Millstone on cobblestone or stone: 2.5%.
uses: Nine make an Emerald in a [[pressure-crucible]] over a heated Blaze Burner.
tips: On average one dust comes from every 20 cobblestone crushed, so an Emerald costs about 180 cobblestone.
facts: Your first one earns Glitter in the Gravel.

name: Netherite Dust
summary: Heavy, dark grains, very rarely left when Crushing Wheels grind netherrack: nine press into Netherite Scrap over a superheated burner.

teach.what: A 1% extra when Crushing Wheels turn netherrack into cinder flour. Nine in a [[pressure-crucible]] over a **superheated** Blaze Burner make one Netherite Scrap.
teach.why: Fully automatable netherite, without mining ancient debris.
teach.when: Mid game, once you can make netherrack (a Mixer over a heated Blaze Burner, cobblestone and 50 mB of lava) and keep a burner superheated with Blaze Cakes.
teach.interacts: Netherrack comes from a [[cobblestone-generator]] plus lava from a [[lava-upgrade|Lava Wellspring]]. The same crushing gives cinder flour (half of [[monster-chow|Monster Chow]]) and [[quartz-dust]] at 5%.
mistakes: Pressing over a merely heated burner. Netherite Scrap needs superheating, so keep the burner fed with Blaze Cakes.
Under-building. At 1%, a Netherite Scrap takes about 900 netherrack on average.

obtain: Crushing Wheels on netherrack: 1% a block, alongside cinder flour (1, plus 50% for a second).
uses: Nine make Netherite Scrap in a [[pressure-crucible]] over a superheated Blaze Burner.
tips: Make netherrack with a Mixer: cobblestone and 50 mB of lava over a heated burner. A cobblestone generator and a Lava Wellspring make the whole chain endless.
facts: Your first one earns One in a Hundred: "Feeling lucky?"

name: Quartz Dust
summary: Pale, sparkly grit from crushing netherrack or blackstone: four press into Nether Quartz.

teach.what: A by-product of Crushing Wheels: 5% from netherrack, 10% from blackstone (which crushes to gravel). Four in a [[pressure-crucible]] over a heated Blaze Burner make one Nether Quartz.
teach.why: Quartz for Create's Rose Quartz, electron tubes and redstone parts, without trips to the Nether. Pressed further, four Nether Quartz make two Amethyst Shards.
teach.when: When you start crushing netherrack for [[netherite-dust]], or build a [[blackstone-generator]].
teach.interacts: A [[blackstone-generator]] gives the better chance. The Nether Quartz can go back into the Crucible (superheated) for amethyst.
mistakes: Pressing it with no heat: Nether Quartz needs a heated burner, amethyst a superheated one.
Crushing netherrack only for quartz. A [[blackstone-generator]] gives twice the chance, and netherrack is better saved for [[netherite-dust]].

obtain: Crushing Wheels on blackstone: 10%.
Crushing Wheels on netherrack: 5%.
uses: Four make Nether Quartz in a [[pressure-crucible]] over a heated Blaze Burner.
Four Nether Quartz then make two Amethyst Shards over a superheated one.
tips: A blackstone line gives about one Nether Quartz per 40 blackstone crushed.

name: FE Coil
summary: Copper wound on a redstone core: the part that lets a machine take Forge Energy, used in Trade Bot and the Netherite Monster Cage.

teach.what: A crafting part. Four copper sheets around a redstone dust make one.
teach.why: Machines that run on Forge Energy need it: [[trade-bot|Trade Bot]]'s winding station and the [[netherite-monster-cage]]'s containment field.
teach.when: When you're ready to build either of those. It's cheap, so make a few once you have copper sheets.
teach.interacts: It goes into Mechanical Crafting recipes. The machines it makes then need a real FE supply, such as a [[lava-generator]] on [[power-lines|Power Lines]].
mistakes: Building an FE machine before you have a generator. The coil only lets the machine take power; something still has to make it.
Crafting it with copper ingots. It takes copper sheets (any `c:plates/copper`), pressed first.

obtain: Crafting table: copper sheets above, below and either side of a redstone dust.
uses: 1 in [[trade-bot|Trade Bot]]'s 5x5 Mechanical Crafting recipe.
2 in the [[netherite-monster-cage]]'s Mechanical Crafting recipe.
facts: Making one earns Coiled and Ready.
tips: Make two extra while you're at it: the Netherite Monster Cage takes two.

name: Capture Bottle
summary: A copper-capped bottle that catches one animal, fish, squid or axolotl, to start an Animal Pen or a Fish Tank.

teach.what: Use it on an animal that breeds (modded ones too), or on cod, salmon, tropical fish, pufferfish, squid, glow squid or an axolotl, and it's caught: the Bottled Animal shows it standing inside and keeps its colour, name and variant.
teach.why: One bottled animal is all an [[animal-pen]] or [[fish-tank]] needs to start a whole herd or school.
teach.when: Your first step into one-block farming. It costs a copper nugget and a glass bottle.
teach.interacts: Use the full bottle on a pen or tank to move the creature in. Animals go in [[animal-pen|Animal Pens]], water creatures in [[fish-tank|Fish Tanks]]; monsters need an [[iron-jar]] instead. Deployers and Dispensers can catch and release with it.
mistakes: Trying to catch a monster. The Capture Bottle refuses it, with a hint: monsters need an [[iron-jar]].
Putting a bottled fish or axolotl in an Animal Pen. Pens refuse water creatures and point you to the Fish Tank.
Trying to take someone else's tamed pet: it can't be caught.
Using an empty bottle on a tank to get a creature back out. That's done from the tank's Wrench screen, which also culls the rest into the output.

specs: Animals that breed, fish, squid, glow squid, axolotls
Monsters, tadpoles, dolphins, other players' pets
obtain: Crafting: a copper nugget on top of a glass bottle.
uses: Use it on a creature to catch it; use the full bottle on the ground to let it out again and get the bottle back.
Use a Bottled Animal on an empty [[animal-pen]] or [[fish-tank]] to start it.
tips: Name an animal before you bottle it: the name and variant carry into the pen's window.
facts: Catching your first animal earns Message in a Bottle: "It seems fine about it".

name: Iron Jar
summary: A jar for catching one monster, at any health, to start a Monster Cage.

teach.what: Use it on any monster a cage takes and it's caught, whatever its health. The jar shows the monster inside. Use it on a [[monster-cage]] to move the monster in, or on the ground to let it out again.
teach.why: One jarred monster starts a whole horde: string, bones, gunpowder and slime without building a dark-room farm.
teach.when: As soon as you have a Deployer: it's an Iron Sheet deployed onto a Glass Bottle.
teach.interacts: Jars go into [[monster-cage|Monster Cages]] and [[flooded-monster-cage|Flooded cages]] of the right tier. Deployers and Dispensers can catch and release with it. A smithing table turns it into a [[netherite-jar]] for Withers.
mistakes: Trying to catch the Wither, a ridden monster, the Warden, the Ender Dragon, a Giant or an Illusioner. None of them fit; the Wither needs a [[netherite-jar]].
Releasing a monster on Peaceful: it's refused.
Letting a full jar burn or blow up. A destroyed jar loses its monster.
Using it on an animal. Animals and fish need a [[capture-bottle]].

specs: Any monster a cage takes, at any health
Its data, name tag included; not its equipment
obtain: A Deployer puts an Iron Sheet on a Glass Bottle (Create's deploying).
uses: Catch a monster, then use the full jar on a [[monster-cage]] that takes it.
Use a full jar on the ground to let the monster out, anywhere but on Peaceful.
Smithing with a Netherite Upgrade template and a netherite ingot makes a [[netherite-jar]].
tips: Catch the monster you want most first: a cage holds one kind only, and emptying it culls the rest.
A Dispenser loaded with empty jars catches the monster in front of it when pulsed: handy beside a spawner.

name: Netherite Jar
summary: The only jar that holds a Wither, and the only way to put one into a Netherite Monster Cage. Fireproof and blast-proof.

teach.what: An [[iron-jar]] smithed with netherite. It catches a Wither at any health, any time after it spawns.
teach.why: It's how a [[contained-wither|Wither]] gets into a [[netherite-monster-cage]], for Nether Stars without a boss fight every time.
teach.when: End game, when you have the Netherite cage built and a real FE grid to hold the field.
teach.interacts: A jarred Wither can only be let out into a Netherite Monster Cage, never into the world. A Deployer holding one can catch a Wither; a Dispenser does nothing with a full one.
mistakes: Trying to release the Wither somewhere else. It only goes into a Netherite cage.
Catching a Wither before the cage has power. Build the grid first: the field takes 2,048 FE a tick from the moment a Wither is inside.

specs: Smithing: Netherite Upgrade template, Iron Jar, netherite ingot
obtain: A smithing table: a Netherite Upgrade smithing template, an [[iron-jar]] and a netherite ingot.
uses: Catch a Wither with it, then use the full jar on a [[netherite-monster-cage]].
tips: Fight the Wither near the cage, so you don't have to carry it far before the jar.

name: Monster Chow
summary: What caged monsters eat: wheat flour, cinder flour and bone meal mixed in a Mixer, three at a time. Edible, badly.

teach.what: The running cost of every [[monster-cage|Monster Cage]]. Each new monster eats 1 (common Overworld monsters), 2 (Nether, End, ocean, pillager-type and modded ones), 4 (rare ones such as evokers, vindicators, ravagers, shulkers and elder guardians) or 64 (a Wither).
teach.why: A cage only brings in monsters while it has chow. Making it from milled ingredients keeps the farm honest: no caged monster drops wheat flour or cinder flour.
teach.when: With your first cage. You need a Millstone or Crushing Wheels for the flours and a Mixer.
teach.interacts: Wheat flour comes from milling wheat (an [[auto-harvester]] grows it), cinder flour from crushing netherrack (the [[netherite-dust]] line makes it anyway), bone meal from skeletons in a cage. Funnels and arms load it into a cage from any side.
mistakes: Running a fast shaft on a thin chow supply. Faster rotation brings monsters in sooner and eats chow just as much faster.
Forgetting the multiplier. A Brass cage of blazes eats twice as fast as one of zombies, and takes twice as long per monster.
Eating it. It's like rotten flesh: 4 hunger with an 80% chance of Hunger.

specs: Mixer, no heat: Wheat Flour + Cinder Flour + Bone Meal = 3
obtain: A Mechanical Mixer, no heat: 1 Wheat Flour, 1 Cinder Flour and 1 Bone Meal make 3.
uses: Put it in a cage's bowl by hand, funnel or arm.
Eat it, if you must: 4 hunger, with an 80% chance of Hunger.

Each bite also has a 25% chance of a **Monster Belch** (a random monster's sound, heard by everyone near) and a 5% chance of **Chow Breath** (10 seconds of Nausea and a puff of green from your mouth).
tips: An Andesite cage of zombies at 64 RPM eats 180 chow an hour: 60 Mixer batches. Size your flour supply from that.

name: Fish Food
summary: What Fish Tank creatures eat: wheat flour, dried kelp and bone meal mixed in a Mixer, four at a time.

teach.what: Every adult in a [[fish-tank]] eats one Fish Food each time it breeds. Out in the world it breeds axolotls, as a Bucket of Tropical Fish does, and fish swim after you while you hold it.
teach.why: Tanks only breed while they have food (and water), so this is the tank's running cost.
teach.when: With your first Fish Tank.
teach.interacts: Wheat flour from milling wheat, dried kelp from smoking kelp (an [[auto-harvester]] grows kelp), bone meal from bones. Funnels load it into a tank from any side.
mistakes: Expecting a full tank of 128 to run on a trickle. Every adult eats one each breeding, so a full tank eats a lot.
Giving tank creatures animal food. Tanks only take Fish Food.

specs: Mixer, no heat: Wheat Flour + Dried Kelp + Bone Meal = 4
obtain: A Mechanical Mixer, no heat: 1 Wheat Flour, 1 Dried Kelp and 1 Bone Meal make 4.
uses: Feed a [[fish-tank]]'s trough by hand, funnel or arm.
Breed wild axolotls with it, or lead fish around while you hold it.
tips: A cod tank at its cap, culled every interval, eats about 770 Fish Food an hour at 64 RPM. Plan the Mixer to match.

name: Intake
summary: The fitting that makes a Fluid Line move fluid: clipped on the side that faces a tank, it draws that tank's fluid in. It replaces the pump.

teach.what: Clip it onto the side of a [[fluid-lines|Fluid Line]] that faces a tank or machine, and it draws that block's fluid into the line. It's the only part of a line that moves fluid. It has a built-in filter: set it to one fluid and it draws only that.
teach.why: Without an Intake, a Fluid Line does nothing. With one, it carries fluid across the whole base with no pump and no stress.
teach.when: With your first Fluid Line.
teach.interacts: It only draws from containers: Create tanks, the [[fluid-wellspring]], machines and other mods' tanks. Two Intakes on one line share its throughput. It never delivers back into the block it draws from.
mistakes: Clipping it on a side that doesn't face a tank: you'll get "Fit the Intake on the side of the line that faces a tank".
Expecting it to suck up a lava lake or the sea. It never draws from fluid in the world; that's still Create's pump and Hose Pulley's job.
Leaving the filter empty on a line where two sources could flow. Set each Intake to its own fluid so the line doesn't switch between them.

specs: A straight Fluid Line, on the side facing a tank
Right-click the line with a bucket; empty hand clears
obtain: Shapeless crafting: a Create Fluid Valve and an Iron Sheet.
uses: Right-click a straight piece of line with it, on the side that faces the source.
Right-click the fitted line with a bucket (or any fluid-holding item) to set the filter; with an empty hand to clear it.
The Wrench takes it off again.
tips: It's the one costly part of a fluid run, since it uses a Fluid Valve. One per source is plenty.
facts: Fitting your first earns Drinking Straw.

name: Valve
summary: A fitting that shuts a Fluid Line on a redstone signal, and throttles it in 10% steps with its wheel.

teach.what: Clip it round a straight piece of [[fluid-lines|Fluid Line]]. A redstone signal shuts it. Right-click turns its wheel a tenth shut; sneak + right-click opens it a tenth.
teach.why: To stop a line when a tank is full, a machine is off, or you're working on it, and to share a source fairly between two lines by holding one back.
teach.when: When you first need control over a line. It costs a Fluid Valve and a copper sheet.
teach.interacts: Past a shut Valve the line's windows show empty. Pair it with a comparator on a tank, or a [[meter]], to switch on demand.
mistakes: Using an empty hand when you meant to open it: plain right-click closes a step, sneak opens one.
Fitting it on a bend or a junction. Fittings go on straight pieces, one per block.

specs: Redstone shuts it; wheel throttles 0 to 100% in 10% steps
obtain: Shapeless crafting: a Create Fluid Valve and a Copper Sheet.
uses: Right-click a straight piece of line with it.
Engineer's Goggles show how far open it is, or "Valve shut by redstone".
tips: A comparator on the tank a line fills, wired to a Valve, shuts the line when the tank is full and saves the source for something else.

name: Filter
summary: A fitting that lets one fluid past and nothing else: for sorting fluids part-way along a Fluid Line.

teach.what: Clip it round a straight piece of [[fluid-lines|Fluid Line]] and set it with a bucket: only that fluid gets past it. Empty, it lets anything past.
teach.why: When one line could carry more than one fluid, Filters make sure each branch only ever gets its own.
teach.when: When you run two sources into one line, or protect a machine that must never get the wrong fluid.
teach.interacts: The [[intake]] has a filter of its own for the source end; the Filter works anywhere along the line. Past a Filter set to another fluid, the windows show empty.
mistakes: Forgetting to set it. An empty Filter lets everything through: goggles say "Filter lets anything past".
Using a Filter where an Intake's own filter would do. If the source is the only place a fluid comes from, set the [[intake]] instead and save the part.

specs: Right-click with a bucket or fluid-holding item; empty hand clears
obtain: Shapeless crafting: a Copper Sheet, Paper and Iron Bars.
uses: Right-click a straight piece of line with it, then set it with a bucket.
tips: One line can carry water to some machines and lava to others if each branch has a Filter set to its own fluid.

name: Meter
summary: A fitting for Fluid or Power Lines whose needle shows the live flow through it. Comparators and Display Links read it.

teach.what: Clip it round a straight piece of [[fluid-lines|Fluid Line]] or [[power-lines|Power Line]]. Its dial shows what's flowing now; goggles give the figure in mB or FE a tick.
teach.why: It answers "is anything moving, and how much?" at a glance, and turns that into redstone.
teach.when: As soon as your lines get long enough that you can't see both ends.
teach.interacts: A comparator reads 0 to 15 by the fraction of the line's throughput that's flowing. Display Links read Meter Flow, Meter Load or a Meter Load Bar onto a board.
mistakes: Reading the comparator as an amount. It's a fraction of the line's own throughput, so the same flow reads lower on brass than on copper.
Fitting it on a junction or a bend. Like every fitting except the power Splitter, it needs a straight piece.

specs: A straight Fluid Line or Power Line
Meter Flow, Meter Load, Meter Load Bar
obtain: Shapeless crafting: a Copper Ingot, an Electron Tube and Glass.
uses: Right-click a straight piece of line with it.
Point a Display Link at it for a live flow board.
tips: A Meter next to a generator's output tells you how close a copper line is to its 4,096 FE cap: time for brass when it reads near 15.

name: Splitter
summary: Decides how a line shares: on a Fluid Line it sets Even, Nearest first or Round robin; on a Power Line junction it ranks the branches First, Second or Last.

teach.what: Two jobs in one item. On a Fluid Line it clips round a straight piece and decides how the ends beyond it share: evenly, nearest first, or one at a time in turn. On a Power Line it sits on a junction of three or four ways (floor, wall or ceiling) and ranks each branch First, Second or Last for when power runs short.
teach.why: Without one, a Fluid Line shares evenly and a Power Line shares evenly between its machines. When there isn't enough to go round, a Splitter decides who goes without.
teach.when: When a short supply starts stopping the wrong machines, or one tank should fill before the others.
teach.interacts: Power branches set First get everything they want before Second, then Last; branches on one level share evenly. Splitters further down a branch rank within it. Its dial points at the First branch (the fork mark when all are level).
mistakes: Right-clicking a power Splitter to change it: that only works on Fluid Lines. A power Splitter's priorities are set in its screen, opened with a Wrench (sneak + Wrench takes it off).
Putting a power Splitter on a straight piece. It goes on a junction, a T or a cross.
Setting everything to First. All First is the same as all Second: even sharing.

obtain: Shapeless crafting: an Electron Tube and a Brass Sheet.
uses: Fluid Line: right-click a straight piece with it, then right-click to cycle its mode.
Power Line: place it on a junction, then Wrench it for its screen. Each row shows a branch, what's down it, and its priority (or Power in).
tips: Put the [[netherite-monster-cage]] on a First branch. When power is short, the Withers' field should be the last thing to go dark.

name: Breaker
summary: A switch for Power Lines: its lever or a redstone signal cuts the power, and it can join a brass run to a copper one.

teach.what: Clip it onto a straight piece of [[power-lines|Power Line]]. Right-click flips its lever; a redstone signal cuts it too. It's the Valve's twin for power.
teach.why: To switch whole circuits on and off, and to step a brass trunk down to copper without going through a pole.
teach.when: When you have more than one circuit, or want a machine room you can shut off.
teach.interacts: To join tiers, run the other tier up to it and wrench that wire's joint with it (same colour): brass then feeds copper through it while it's on, never the other way. The cable under its housing changes to show it.
mistakes: Expecting copper to feed brass through it. Brass feeds copper only.
Trying to join two colours at a Breaker. Two colours never join.

specs: Brass to copper, once the joint is wrenched
obtain: Shapeless crafting: a Lever and an Electron Tube.
uses: Right-click a straight piece of Power Line with it; right-click again to flip the lever.
tips: A Breaker with a lever is the quickest way to shut off a whole machine room while you rebuild it.

name: Bountiful
summary: An enchantment for the Auto Harvester only, I to III: each level grows its plant 50% faster.

teach.what: Each level makes the [[auto-harvester]]'s plant grow 50% faster: 1.5x at I, 2x at II, 2.5x at III. The 4-second harvest itself doesn't change.
teach.why: The harvester always uses 512 SU and runs no faster with more speed, so Bountiful is the only way to speed it up.
teach.when: As soon as you have an Auto Harvester and a Librarian to trade with.
teach.interacts: Put it on the harvester item with an anvil; it stays when the harvester is broken and placed again. Its screen shows the level.
mistakes: Looking for it in an enchanting table. Tables never offer it: buy the book from a Librarian.
Putting it on a pen or cage. The anvil refuses: each farm enchantment fits only its own machines.

obtain: Librarians: in their usual random enchanted-book trades, and as an extra Apprentice trade at a random level, priced like their own books (emeralds and a book).
Two books of the same level combine on an anvil into the next level, as vanilla books do.
uses: Combine the book with an [[auto-harvester]] item on an anvil.
facts: An Auto Harvester with Bountiful III earns Overgrown.
tips: Bountiful matters most on trees: an 80-second sapling drops to 32 seconds at III.

name: Fruitful
summary: An enchantment for the Animal Pens and Fish Tanks, I to III: each level breeds and grows the herd or school 50% faster.

teach.what: Each level makes an [[animal-pen]] or [[fish-tank]] breed, and its young grow up, 50% faster: 1.5x, 2x and 2.5x.
teach.why: A pen breeds every five minutes at vanilla's pace. Fruitful III cuts that to two minutes, so a herd fills up in a fraction of the time.
teach.when: With your first pen or tank, once you've found a Librarian selling it.
teach.interacts: It works on the Animal Pen, Brass Animal Pen, Fish Tank and Brass Fish Tank, and stays on the block when it's broken. The pens' stress doesn't change; food is eaten faster, since breeding is.
mistakes: Feeding a Fruitful pen as you fed a plain one. Faster breeding means faster eating: keep the trough topped up by funnel.
Putting it on a Monster Cage. Cages take [[monstrous]] instead.

specs: +50% breeding and growing speed per level (config)
obtain: Librarians: random enchanted-book trades, and an extra Apprentice trade at a random level, for emeralds and a book.
uses: Combine the book with a pen or tank item on an anvil.
facts: An Animal Pen with Fruitful III earns Be Fruitful and Multiply.
tips: Put Fruitful on the Brass pen first: with 512 animals, every minute saved is a bigger litter.

name: Monstrous
summary: An enchantment for every Monster Cage, I to III: each level makes monsters arrive 50% faster, Netherite cage included.

teach.what: Each level makes new monsters arrive 50% faster in any [[monster-cage]]: 1.5x, 2x, 2.5x. Chow per monster and stress don't change.
teach.why: It's more drops from the same cage, without more rotation. On the [[netherite-monster-cage]] it takes Nether Stars from 3 an hour to 7.5 at Monstrous III and 256 RPM.
teach.when: Once a cage is running and you can keep up with its chow.
teach.interacts: It works on the Monster Cage, Brass Monster Cage, both Flooded cages and the Netherite cage, and stays when the cage is broken. Because monsters arrive faster, [[monster-chow|Monster Chow]] goes faster too.
mistakes: Forgetting the chow bill. Monstrous III eats chow 2.5 times as fast.
Trying it on a pen or tank: the anvil refuses. Those take [[fruitful]].

obtain: Librarians: random enchanted-book trades, and an extra Apprentice trade at a random level, for emeralds and a book.
uses: Combine the book with a cage item on an anvil.
tips: On the Netherite cage, Monstrous III takes a Wither from every 20 minutes to every 8 at 256 RPM.
